newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia Petronas denies interest in Chandra Asri.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Petronas denies interest in Chandra Asri.

text.p: Malaysia's state oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) does not have any plans to take a stake in Indonesia's PT Chandra Asri Petrochemical Centre, a Petronas official told Reuters on Monday.
He denied a report in Jakarta's Bisnis Indonesia daily which cited an unnamed source saying Petronas would soon buy a large stake in the petrochemical project from timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu.

"Petronas denies the report," the official said when asked for comment. "We confirm that there are no plans to take any stake, whether big or small, in Chandra Asri. We are also not studying the possibility."

According to one source quoted by the newspaper, an agreement would soon be sealed to allow Petronas to take the stake but it did not specify the exact number of shares that Petronas would take or the value of each share.
Bisnis Indonesia cited another source as saying that Petronas would buy more than 30-50 percent of Prajogo's stake in Chandra Asri.

Chandra Asri, before changing its status to a foreign investment company, was 40 percent controlled by Prajogo Pangestu, 25 percent by Indonesian businessman Henry Pribadi and 35 percent by President Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo.
Following the changes, Siemene International holds 65 percent, Stallion Co Ltd 10 percent and Japan Indonesia Petrochemical Corp 25 percent.
The Bisnis Indonesia report, citing sources, said Prajogo holds 10 percent, while Bambang holds 60 percent, following the changes.
Chandra Asri has an annual production capacity of around 520,000 tonnes of ethylene, 243,000 tonnes of propylene, 300,000 tonnes of polyethelene and pyrolysis gasoline.
